card.name: Digits inside dose numbers
card.fires_on: The decimal point or a digit inside a number in a dose or volume table, such as the point in 1.5 mg/kg or the digit in 1280/36 mcg. It fires most where the number is a half-step or a doubled value.

modes.label: Decimal point
modes.description: The decimal point after a leading digit in a dose, volume or ratio value.

modes.label: Digit in strength pair
modes.description: A digit inside a combination-strength or dose-reduction number.
modes.example: ADA, if tolerated. For patients known to be poor metabolizers of CYP2D6 : Reduce dose to 441 mg from <<6>>62 mg

card.writes: It suppresses the word half and its Chinese equivalents, so it seems to steer away from half-amount wording after a number.
card.plain: It fires inside dose numbers in tables, especially at the decimal point, where the next digits are being chosen.
